eli5.why: Web pages are stiff. They are boxes, a few fixed looks, and one long scroll. Eido wants pages that bend, like clay, so they fit the person reading, but only in ways that person can see and undo.
eli5.modules: Eido is a toolbox with six tools. You can pick up one tool without taking the rest, like using only the hammer from a toolbox.
eli5.d1: A style is like a paint mix of a few base looks. A triangle lets you slide between them, and the three amounts always add to one. Colours mix around a wheel, so two reds stay red.
eli5.d2: Letters can be a list of dots, like a connect-the-dots card. Shapes made by math stay sharp when you zoom. A page can also notice how fast you read and soften when you slow down.
eli5.d3: Imagine a sealed note. The note is tiny, and it has a stamp. Before you read it, you check the stamp matches. No stamp, and you do not trust the note.
eli5.d4: Skin goes red when you push on it. A screen can show stress too. While a system is calm, edges pulse softly. Near its limit, glow and grain change, so you see the strain without a popup.
eli5.d5: You remember where your bedroom is, not how far down a hallway it sits. Eido imagines a few named rooms. Pick a room and both the words and the picture change. This idea is only a design so far.
eli5.d6: When you race through a page, it notices. Then it can ripple to slow you down, or shrink to a short version. Read carefully and it calms. You can switch it off, and nothing leaves your browser.
eli5.fields: Picture a map where bigger circles mean bigger numbers. Each thing in the picture, like size and place, tells you one fact only. The computer works out the sizes first, then hands the drawing tool exact boxes.
eli5.in-use: Eido is not just an idea. A website, this site, and a research project already use pieces of it. This page you are reading is one of them: it shrinks if you skim.
